title: Exercise-angina–ST-depression interaction failed to improve Cleveland-to-Hungary prediction of angiographic disease
abstract: A source-centered exercise-angina by ST-depression interaction was evaluated against a fixed nonlinear additive model of conventional clinical and exercise-test measures in public UCI Heart Disease cohorts. Training used 303 Cleveland patients; frozen confirmation used 294 Hungarian patients. Brier score worsened from 0.13968 to 0.14395 (delta +0.00426; paired target bootstrap 95% interval +0.00192 to +0.00661). A joint source-refit/target bootstrap interval included zero (−0.00218 to +0.01666), so universal inferiority is not established. Linear, complete-case, sex-stratified, ST-slope-adjusted and duplicate-removal checks also showed no point-estimate improvement. This negative, limited transport test does not test the full Duke treadmill score or establish absence of symptom–ECG biological information.
